flags: minor: choice D ($30) just repeats the $30 in the stem, so it is a weak distractor
Q039-02.notes: 5(1.2r) = 4r + 30 -> 2r = 30, r = 15 (old rate, which is choice A as a trap); new rate = 18.

Q039-03.notes: Origin: 4x-3y = 0 < 12. A: 11 < 12, so same side. B: 13, C: 15, D: 15, all > 12.

Q039-04.notes: d/50 + d/30 = 4 -> 8d/150 = 4 -> d = 75. 160 and 80 come from averaging the speeds to 40 mph.

Q039-05.notes: Axis x=1; f(1) = k(2)(-2) = -4k. One x-intercept means the vertex of g is on the x-axis: -4k + 8 = 0 -> k = 2. (Discriminant check: 4k^2 - 4k(8-3k) = 16k^2 - 32k = 0 -> k = 2, since k is nonzero.)

Q039-06.notes: (x^(3/2))^(1/2) = x^(3/4) = 8 -> x = 8^(4/3) = 16. Testing the choices also works quickly.

Q039-07.notes: Vertex (-b/2, c - b^2/4). Quadrant IV: -b/2 > 0 -> b < 0, and c - b^2/4 < 0 -> b^2 > 4c. B is not required: with b=-4, c=1 the vertex is (2,-3). C and D have the wrong sign of b.

flags: minor: B and D are mirror images, and A and C are easy to rule out once a student notices the t/2, so it comes down to a choice between B and D
Q039-08.notes: f decreases 5%/yr. g has an annual factor of 0.9^(1/2) = 0.9487, about a 5.13%/yr decrease, which is greater than f's. C is wrong because g's 10% drop is every 2 years.

Q039-09.notes: Multiply all y-values by 100, so both slope and intercept scale: y = 250x + 1000. B is the trap of scaling only the slope.

Q039-10.notes: Speed is proportional to 1/pace: 8/7.5 = 1.0667, so a 6.67% increase. A (6.25%) is the decrease in pace, which is the trap. C and D are ratio-style distractors.

Q039-12.notes: Triangles ABD and ACB are similar (they share angle A, and angle ABD = angle ACB). AD/AB = AB/AC -> AD = 36/9 = 4, so DC = 9 - 4 = 5.
